description: Issue #839: when a program contains BOTH kinds of declaration-slot collision, the first one in SOURCE ORDER halts it. Here a duplicate `tally` on line 4 precedes a built-in `define forward` on line 7, and the duplicate is what is reported — the run stops there, so the later `ol-reserved-word` is never produced. This is the ordering property, deliberately separated from the *priority* property (`ol-reserved-word` beats `ol-duplicate-definition` when ONE name is both), which is a check-stage concern because `check()` reports every finding while `execute()` stops at the first. The mirror program — the `define forward` block first, then the duplicated `tally` — reports `ol-reserved-word` at the built-in declaration instead and never reaches the duplicate; it is pinned as a unit test (`execute-declaration-slots.test.mjs`, "the first collision in source order halts the run, whichever code it carries") rather than as a second fixture, since the two differ only in block order.
